In a previous org, I had a boss put me on a PIP. This was completely unsubstantiated and, I suspect, motivated by the fact that she just didn’t like me. Fortunately, my org had a program called "360 evaluation" that sent out surveys to colleagues throughout the org (executive stakeholders, team members, clients, etc). I escalated to her boss and insisted that I get a 360 eval because my boss had no concrete examples of why I was on PIP (mainly platitudes of her feelings of how I was performing). As an aside, I was open to specific feedback on how I could improve, but she didn’t have any to give me. No way to get off PIP if it is just vibes. When the eval came back, I ranked extremely highly from all levels, including getting praise from senior executives. That got my PIP removed immediately. She left my team to work on another team shortly thereafter.

Bottom line, if you are getting PIP'd and you think it is unsubstantiated,  gather data and fight back!

Ive worked in warehouses and the logistics/transportation field since i was 16. Everything from picking, forklift operator and driving a vans and box trucks for delivery. 39 now and finally starting a job thats out of this industry. 

It is absolutely soul, and body crushing. You never actually get anywhere. You are worked to death day in and day out, 40-up to 80 hours a week, every week. Youll never move up. Your always looked down on. Any supervisor/management positions are nearly always brought in from the outside with people with experience and degrees. 

It dont matter how hard you work, how many hours a day or week you work, how your numbers look nothing. I worked for YEARS with no time off. No vacations, every holiday, no call outs nothing. And what do you get? A broken body and broken mind. Thats it. You work your life away and your body into the ground until you physically cant do it anymore. My entire back is destroyed from lower all the way to the base of my neck. Alot of days i can hardly physically move and its been like that for over a decade. 

These jobs are absolutely brutal. When i first started it seemed great. I was making double or triple right out of high school (well even before during summer breaks, not legal i know but it was a different time then) then most others i knew working fast food or generic retail, and didnt have to talk with or deal with any customers. Seemed great. Problem is though, the pay and benefits aint there anymore. What used to be a decent job running a forklift (once you grinded your ways to get on the lifts "full time", which it never actually is anyway) is now not much better pay then just above minumum wage. Companies started finding out they can just bring temps in, half ass train them with a couple hour in house training class, and pay them way less. This completely shifted the whole landscape. Now, 20 years experience operating dozens of pieces of equipment?  Thats nice, you might get $15-17/hr if your lucky. 

What else they dont tell you and can arguably be the worst part, is that once your in, its hard to get out. Your stuck. Nobody else wants to look at you for anything else when thats all youve done. Other skills dont matter. Any kind of additional education or certs you may have somehow find time to get dont matter. They see youve just always been a warehouse worker they dont want anything to do with you. So you just keep doing it cause you still need to eat. You still have bills to pay. Nobody else wants to give you the time of day and your facing a life of being stigmatized and looked down on because of it. And you can rarely ever escape. Thats why even in these comments you hear of people doing this work for 20 or 30 years. They are trapped. 

Finally landed an IT roll. 30 years of knowledge and experience working on and constantly learning computers finally got me an entry level IT position.  And even though i still may never rise up to 6 figure salaries in that industry at this point, i am so glad ive finally broken free from warehousing.  Even with it being entry level im still starting at a higher wage then i was at after years at my last job. With no heat, no working in the pouring rain, no dealing with traffic, and no back breaking labor. 

And thats my rant. If your in warehousing now, get out as soon as you can. If your thinking about it for quick and easy cash, have a backup plan. Have an out ready. Dont let yourself get stuck until literally the day you die. Cause ill promise you this. A lifelong of warehouse work, you will not make it to retirement.

Most of the delivery drivers do not work directly for Amazon.  Amazon outsourced most of this to 3rd party companies so that they can say it's not them and create distance between the driver and Amazon.  I worked with 2 clients that have contracted with Amazon.  Collectively, they have about 60 trucks on the road. Yes, Amazon provides the trucks, the technology, the business model and more.  However, everything provided must be reimbursed back to Amazon and they take their money off the top -- before the contractor sees it. Have your backpack and/or handbag with you as you approach your supervisor. 

Have enough savings to cover at least a month without pay.
